items.title: Colouring a Poisson--Dirichlet process recovers the Dirichlet distribution: a probabilistic proof
items.author: Tony Haddad; Dimitris Koukoulopoulos
items.work: On Arratia's coupling and the Dirichlet law for the factors of a random integer
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `prop:probabilistic dirichlet law` at source lines 1121-1128: colouring the points of a Poisson--Dirichlet process independently with probabilities alpha_j yields a random vector distributed according to Dir(alpha). The author's proof (source lines 1130-1148), repeated from Donnelly and Tavare because the Poisson representation is needed later, is a two-tool computation: the colouring theorem turns the single Poisson process into k independent processes of intensities alpha_m e^{-x}/x dx (lines 1131-1138), and Campbell's theorem evaluates the Laplace transform of each coloured sum, producing the integral of (e^{sx}-1)e^{-x}/x whose value -alpha_m log(1-s) identifies a Gamma(alpha_m,1) law (lines 1139-1143). The Dirichlet conclusion then follows by normalising the independent Gamma sums (lines 1144-1147). Both cited theorems are structural, and neither the colouring representation nor the generating-function computation is visible from the statement.
